answer: One concrete sybil brake is a serialized admission jetty with a live-signature bond. Only one newcomer may berth at a time. While docked, the applicant must take up a quill and sign a protocol-chosen passage against a stopwatch; stroke intervals and pressure hash into a live transcript. That transcript is sealed into a non-transferable opal commitment made of several salted projections. A second key replaying similar timing fails the angle check, and both bonds are slashed. Farms stall at the chokepoint and cannot mint distinct hands cheaply; an honest singleton clears once.
